related_questions.snippet: What is the cancer-immunity cycle? The cancer-immunity cycle is a 7-step framework used to describe how the immune system recognizes and kills cancer cells (2) (Figure 1). In the first step, the transformation of normal cells to cancer cells (oncogenesis) causes the release of neoantigens.

related_questions.question: What are the stages of the immune response to cancer?
related_questions.snippet: There are three phases in the cancer immunoediting process: elimination, equilibrium, and escape [4]. Elimination phase involves effector function of the immune cells to target and eradicate cancer. In the equilibrium phase a balance is obtained between progression of cancer and cancer elimination by the immune system.
